step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture represents a serverless application modernization effort for American Commercial Barge Line (ACBL) transitioning from a legacy VB6 and Oracle database system. Legacy data changes are captured via AWS DMS and published to Amazon SNS, which triggers an Ingestion Lambda function to reformat relational data into a single-table DynamoDB pattern using an adjacency list model. The web application features an Angular Frontend SPA authenticated via Amazon Cognito. AppSync acts as the GraphQL API layer, integrating permissions from Cognito and orchestrating data resolvers across multiple microservices: a primary Lambda microservice interfacing with DynamoDB and a secondary Lambda microservice fetching river flow and flooding data from the USGS.

edges.notes: DMS pushes database change updates to SNS.
SNS triggers the ingestion Lambda function.
Ingestion Lambda formats and writes synchronized relational data into DynamoDB using adjacency list patterns.
Angular frontend sends user login request to Cognito.
Cognito issues authentication token to the frontend.
Cognito token context evaluates user permissions and directive access in AppSync.
Frontend sends GraphQL queries and mutations to AppSync.
AppSync invokes core microservice Lambda function as a GraphQL resolver.
Microservice Lambda queries single-table DynamoDB for application data.
AppSync invokes USGS weather Lambda microservice.
USGS weather Lambda returns river flow and flood data to AppSync.
AppSync consolidates and returns unified GraphQL payload to Angular application.
